candidates.review: Retain native const inode in fsverity_info and explicit non-const inode argument to verification. Native callers already provide the live inode; removing const and reducing an argument only prepares the later cached-info refactor. The same block hashing, signature checks and read operations remain. All three touched core files equal pinned LTS at this review.

Retain native inode/folio/bio-based verification helpers with internal info lookup. Complete cross-filesystem patch reviewed: the change moves lookup into buffer, btrfs, ext4 and F2FS callers without adding verification. Native direct inode pointer lookup avoids the proposed hash-table cost; native callers still verify buffer offsets, full folios, bios, decompressed pages and holes. Keep the explicit F2FS large-folio subrange adaptation already reviewed. No userspace or vendor hook interface depends on relocating this lookup; btrfs disabled in SDK. Native publication acquire and inode-owned lifetime remain.

Keep native per-filesystem inode-owned verity pointers with release/acquire publication and cleanup, rather than global rhashtable lookup. All affected pointer fields, zero initialization, inode_info_offs and cleanup calls are present in the port. Native fsverity_active tests initialized info (not merely S_VERITY), including enable/open races. The change trades per-inode storage for global lookup/allocation and earlier publication; it does not add an Android userspace operation, verification algorithm or vendor hook. Retaining the LTS representation preserves its existing verification/enable failure semantics and avoids a new global lifetime dependency. This is representation minimization, not historical binary-KMI retention; eight bytes of native pointer storage per enabled-filesystem inode remain.

The verification-context inode remains used by native fsverity_verify_pending_blocks when calling verify_data_block. Its removal is cleanup only after the omitted argument-reduction refactor. Preserve the actual live native field, initialization and use; dropping it alone would break verification, not improve security.

The native fsverity_verify_page helper still has configured F2FS compression verification consumers in compress.c and data.c. Their page-sized compressed mappings remain excluded from large folios; other noncompressed bios/holes use the separately adapted native length/offset helpers. Keep this wrapper and its native core delegation rather than removing a still-used API based on the later ACK consumer conversion. No data verification is omitted.

This fixes a cross-inode hash-chain UAF introduced by f706f34d4749. That hash table is not selected: native fsverity_get_info directly loads the inode-owned pointer, fsverity_free_info removes no shared chain, and other inodes cannot traverse this object during lookup. Full fix and predecessor examined. Retain native inode-lifetime cleanup; applying an RCU union/callback without the hash table is not required to preserve this fix effect. This is a concrete missing-precondition analysis, not a claim that all possible verity lifetime races are ruled out.
